svg.text: K5 Ram-and-die column with piston vessels
Every shape is “push through a die and cut off”; food only falls. A frying book flips, one shuttle carries.
wall width 1770 mm (1170 without oven) · 600 deep · 2000 high
TOP VIEW (deck level, turret at z 1300)
frying book above: leaf L | leaf R
4/8 Carousel sets the Ø80 former under it; 7 mm of ram per patty, wire cuts, pucks drop
5/8 Shuttle sets the pan of patties into leaf L of the frying book
7/8 Shuttle carries the finished pan into the oven (lift door) to keep warm for hand-over
Meanwhile the 9 L pot (mash) turns under its fixed scraper on rear L.
Pans, pots and tools go to the central ware washer; tubes and dies are washed in place.
1/8 Box docks and tilts: mince, roll, egg slide down the chute into the tube at FILL
2/8 Turret turns 120°: the filled tube travels to PRESS on its own blank cap
3/8 Ram takes the knead plunger: back-extrusion mixes the mass (30 strokes, 2 min)
4/8 Carousel sets the Ø80 former under it; 7 mm of ram per patty, wire cuts, pucks drop
5/8 Shuttle sets the pan of patties into leaf L of the frying book: 170 °C, 4 min
6/8 Book flip: leaf R closes over L, both turn 180°, L returns – all patties turned in 6 s
7/8 Shuttle carries the finished pan into the oven (lift door) to keep warm for hand-over
8/8 Clean in place: piston pigs the bore; at SERVICE the spray dasher washes 55 °C, then 85 °C
